summary.intent: Recover a previously discussed Phase 37 (parallel batch upload pipeline) that was added during a prior session but never committed, then capture implementation decisions via the GSD discuss-phase workflow.
summary.outcome: Phase 37 context was fully discussed and captured in 37-CONTEXT.md with locked decisions on concurrency model, SDK API shape, Web Worker encryption, error handling, and scope boundary. STATE.md was updated and files committed.

repo: Phase 37 existed only as uncommitted local changes (ROADMAP.md modified, phase dir untracked) after the previous session — planning artifacts were discussed but never committed to a branch.
The current upload pipeline in useDropUpload.ts loops sequentially; each file calls client.uploadFile() which does encrypt→pin→publish as one atomic unit, resulting in N IPNS publishes for N files.
withOperation() in the SDK serializes all operations — attempting concurrent uploadFile() calls would just queue them, making parallelism at the web layer impossible without SDK changes.

Desktop FUSE uploads are fundamentally single-file (macOS/Windows calls release() per file individually), so a batch upload_files() Rust SDK method would not benefit the desktop app without a separate write-coalescing FUSE layer.

The SDK's internal folderTree state and withOperation() serialization mean batching must live inside the SDK to remain safe — consumer-orchestrated decomposition (Option B) creates orphaned CIDs and sequence number conflict risks.
Stale-children race window exists in any batch approach: folder.children read at batch start can be stale if another device publishes during encrypt+pin. Mitigation is re-read-before-publish.

code.finding: Sequential file upload loop — iterates files one-by-one, calling client.uploadFile() per file. This is the primary target for replacement with a parallel batch call.
uploadFile() does encrypt+pin+publish as one atomic unit inside withOperation() serialization — cannot be parallelized externally without breaking folder consistency.
FUSE release() callback handles each file individually — no batch context available at this layer, so desktop cannot benefit from batch publishing without a write-coalescing buffer layer.
Rust SDK uses a queue model for upload operations — would need a new upload_files() batch entry point for API parity, but FUSE layer won't use it without additional coalescing work.
